title: Fixed-seed cyclic rank as reduced inverse-root span
shortTitle: Fixed-seed cyclic rank from inverse roots
oneLine: A conditional theorem turns fixed-seed cyclic rank into a count of independent inverse-root functions, classifies every indecomposable rank-one to rank-three phase, and exposes block fusion as the remaining compositional obstruction.
abstract: This anonymous, unrefereed candidate studies the differential system generated by the fixed class [dx] for a complex polynomial exponential phase. Conditional on the fixed-seed stationary-phase bridge established in the parent release, it proves that the cyclic rank equals the dimension of the reduced constant span of the inverse roots. The result gives an arbitrary-degree classification for indecomposable phases of rank at most three: powers have rank one, Chebyshev phases rank two, and indecomposable quartics rank three. A finite exact reducer computes cyclic rank for trusted rational polynomial inputs. Right-factor heredity is proved, but a degree-twelve rank-three example shows that symmetry can fuse separate root blocks under composition, so the full decomposable classification remains open. Producer-side replay and internal review tracks pass. No independent reproduction, formal verification, external specialist review, editorial peer review, or novelty or priority determination has occurred.
narration: An exponential integral can generate a differential equation when it is differentiated repeatedly. This candidate asks a simple version of that question: how many genuinely different directions are produced by one chosen starting form? Conditional on the stationary-phase bridge established in the parent Evidence Press release, the answer can be read from the polynomial's inverse branches. Remove the average shared by all inverse roots, then count how many independent inverse-root functions remain. That count is the fixed-seed cyclic rank. For polynomials that cannot be decomposed into lower-degree maps, the low-rank picture is complete in every degree. Powers have rank one. Chebyshev phases have rank two. Indecomposable quartics have rank three. The package also includes an exact calculator for trusted rational polynomial inputs. Composition creates the unresolved case. A degree-twelve example has rank three because a symmetry makes three normally separate root blocks coincide. The candidate therefore does not claim a complete classification for decomposable phases. Instead, it identifies block fusion under polynomial composition as the next problem. The public package contains a ten-page paper, source code, a complete file manifest, byte-identical ordinary and optimized replay receipts, internal mathematical reviews, and scoped prior-art records. These are producer-side checks, not independent verification. The work is anonymous and unrefereed. It has not been formally verified, externally reviewed by specialists, conventionally peer reviewed, or established as novel or first. This is an Evidence Press audio briefing, released 9 August 2026. The voice is AI-generated, and the audio is not additional mathematical evidence.

problem.name: Fixed-seed cyclicity for polynomial exponential periods

keyResults: Conditional on the parent fixed-seed stationary-phase bridge, q(P,dx) equals the dimension of the reduced constant inverse-root span for every complex polynomial phase of degree at least two.
For indecomposable polynomial phases in arbitrary degree, q at most three occurs exactly for powers with q=1, Chebyshev phases with q=2, and indecomposable quartics with q=3, up to affine changes.
A finite exact twisted-de-Rham Krylov reducer computes the fixed-seed cyclic rank for trusted rational polynomial and amplitude inputs and returns exact independence or dependence witnesses.
Every right factor inherits the cyclic-rank upper bound, but P=(x^4+x)^3 has q=3 because symmetry fuses three root-block spans.
The complete decomposable low-rank classification is not claimed; equivariant block fusion under Ritt moves is the stated frontier.
evidence: A 10-page anonymous candidate paper and canonical Markdown; a finite exact SymPy reducer; an 86-entry static manifest that includes nested audit manifests; byte-identical ordinary and optimized producer receipts; fixed-target hash checks; exact Krylov, composition-mutation and independently written clean-room control tracks; held-out implementation checks; internal fixed-text stationary-phase and polynomial-monodromy reviews; a conductor-span follow-up audit; scoped primary-source prior-art ledgers; a rights map; and byte-identical GitHub and Zenodo release assets. This evidence establishes availability, package integrity and producer-side replay, not independent theorem verification.

Extend the fixed-seed criterion beyond dx to nonconstant amplitudes, relative or logarithmic families, and multivariate twisted complexes.
